cases.name: tampered-entry-bundle
cases.says: one byte of one entry changed: the bundle still frames, and the tree it builds is not the one the checkpoint is signed over

cases.name: missing-entry-bundle
cases.says: a log that will not serve its entries cannot be replayed, and a verifier must refuse rather than report what it has

cases.name: consistent-tampered-log
cases.says: the entries and the hash tile are tampered *together*, so the served log agrees with itself and disagrees with the head the checkpoint is signed over: only rebuilding the tree and comparing that head can refuse it

cases.name: tampered-hash-tile
cases.says: one byte of one leaf hash changed: the entries and the signed head are untouched, so a verifier that reaches the head without opening `tile/0/...` sees nothing wrong, and serves the corrupt tile onward to peers asking it for proofs

cases.name: overfull-entry-bundle
cases.says: the bundle decodes but holds one more entry than the checkpoint size and its path imply

comment: a served log is a directory, so each case names the path to replace with `file`, the paths to replace with `files`, or the path to delete with `remove`, over an otherwise honest copy of `served-large/`. Every one MUST be refused, with the SPEC §10.1 code `codes` names for it

consistent-tampered-log.says: that comparison is what binds the entries to the head

missing-entry-bundle.says: any file a later step needs and cannot fetch

overfull-entry-bundle.says: A partial bundle holds **exactly** the number of entries its path declares

tampered-entry-bundle.says: that comparison is what binds the entries to the head
